title: Sattva: Meaning and Context
excerpt: Sattva is one of three qualities in a classical Indian scheme, associated with clarity or lightness, beside rajas and tamas.

quick_answer.question: What does Sattva mean?
quick_answer.answer: Sattva is the quality of clarity, lightness, or goodness in the three-guna scheme. It is not a superfood and not a personality type from a quiz.

intro: Sattva is one guna, a strand or quality. The usual trio is sattva, rajas, and tamas: clarity, activity, and inertia, in a common gloss.

sections.heading: What does Sattva mean?
sections.content:
The Gita and Samkhya-influenced yoga use the scheme to talk about mind and nature. The glosses are approximate. A food tradition later called some diets sattvic. That dietary layer is not the whole philosophy, and it is not a medical nutrition plan.

The neighboring page is [ancient wisdom](/topics/ancient-wisdom/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: Where does the word come from?
sections.content:
Wellness writing often says be more sattvic and means be calm and buy lighter products. The classical term sits inside a psychology of bondage and release. Yoga philosophy pages are the longer route into that psychology.

A wider map lives at the [yoga topic](/topics/yoga/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: How is the word misused?
sections.content:
If you meet the word, learn the trio, not a shopping list. Clarity is not the same as moral superiority. A text that ranks the gunas is making a philosophical claim.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [yoga philosophy](/articles/what-is-yoga-philosophy/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Do not treat a sattvic diet as a cure. Do not rank people by how pure their groceries look. The guna is not a blood test.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: Sattva has a traditional job that popular English often widens.
Context decides which school is speaking.
This entry defines the word and points to a longer page.

faq.question: Is Sattva a scientific term?
faq.answer: No. It is a category in classical thought, not a biomarker.

faq.question: Where is the longer page?
faq.answer: Read the Gita in a cited translation and the yoga philosophy page.
